hypothesis: Add one wider-N prefill autotune candidate, 128x128 w8 num_stages=2 (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2), to the existing 8 _attn_fwd configs (all kept unchanged). Same key, kernel body, grid, fp16 K/V pre-pass and decode path.
rationale: The prefill kernel runs 128x64 w8 s2 at ~68% of the fp16-acc mma peak, 1 CTA/SM, with lockstep softmax/fold phases exposing the tensor pipe. Per 64 KV columns each thread pays a full acc fold (64 cvt + 64 FFMA), an alpha exp2, a q reload from smem (4 KB/warp ldmatrix), loop/barrier overhead and two cp.async waits. A 128-wide KV tile pays those once per 128 columns, halving the non-mma per-flop overhead of the fold and loop, while the per-element softmax cost and the mma count stay the same. The causal diagonal is one masked 128x128 tile, the same waste as today's two 128x64 tiles. Notes (exp 17) show num_stages=2 single-buffers K/V here (128x64 s2 = 32 KB q + 32 KB K/V = 64 KB), so 128x128 s2 should be 32 KB q + 32 KB K + 32 KB V = 96 KB, under the 99 KB limit. This is new: exp 3 tried only 64x128 w8 s1, and exp 14 tried only 128x128 w8 s1 (no prefetch, so load latency was exposed). Exp 14 also ran before exp 15 removed the in-loop bf16->fp16 converts, which used registers and conversion ops. The autotuner keeps HEAD's configs, so if the wider tile spills (more score registers: 64 fp32 instead of 32 per thread), it is not picked.
expected_effect: If 128x128 s2 compiles without heavy spills, the tuner picks it for prefill_4096..32768 and those rows get ~2-5% faster (most at 16k/32k, the thinnest prefill margins). prefill_2048 is about the same, and decode is unchanged. If it spills or does not fit, the tuner keeps 128x64 s2 and the score stays within noise.
